Overall, very shady practices and poor service. I would strongly advise people to avoid this place.

featured_reviews.name: Karthik Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
"I traveled from very far specifically to visit Rekdee - Taste of the Streets in Mulund for their late night food. The experience was a masterclass in how inconsistent management and staff can drive away genuine customers.

The Logical Contradiction:
Upon arrival, the boy at the counter informed me that Misal Pav was not available, but Tari Pav was. When I questioned the logic—given that both dishes share the exact same Tari (curry) and Pav—he failed to provide a valid reason. He then claimed a specific '12 AM to 4 AM' rule where Misal Pav is simply not served. I initially accepted this as a business policy maybe thinking that tarri pav has more profit and it consumes less tari as compared to a misal so they can make around 4-5 tari pavs instead of making 1 misal for profit, choosing to be reasonable and patient.

The Blatant Bias:
The situation changed 10 minutes later when a different family arrived. It was clear the management was partial to this specific group. Suddenly, the '12 AM to 4 AM' rule vanished, and the same staff member announced he was taking 'last orders' for Misal Pav for them. When confronted, he shamelessly claimed the Misal had 'magically' come back into stock. Only after being caught in this lie did he dismissively say, 'If you want now, we can give you,' which entirely missed the point of my concern regarding fair treatment.

The Linguistic Insult & Cowardice:
When I advised the staff that rules should be consistent for everyone, the boy cowardly hid behind the owner, claiming he was just following orders—despite being the one who originally gave me the 'lecture.' To make matters worse, both the owner and the boy began speaking in Gujarati, assuming I wouldn't understand their comments about a 'mess being created.' They were visibly stunned when I informed them that I understood every word of their mockery.

The ‘Go Ahead and Write’ Dare:
When I told the staff that such an unprofessional experience deserved a public review, the boy arrogantly responded with, 'Yeah, go ahead and write.'
To the Owner: Here is the review your staff requested. It is disappointing to see an owner stand by while staff lies to customers and then joins them in mocking a guest in a different language. Petrol and time were wasted on a recommendation that clearly doesn't value its patrons

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mani’ Cafe is unfortunately not a pleasant place to eat. There is no proper seating arrangement, so most people have to stand and eat. The only reason the place remains crowded is because there are very few other options nearby, so people end up coming here anyway.

The food quality is also disappointing. Most dishes are excessively oily, and I would strongly suggest avoiding the sabudana khichdi and pohe. The only somewhat acceptable item is the tea, but even that is inconsistent because a different boy prepares it every day, so the taste keeps changing.

Another issue is the poor crowd management. Beggars often approach and disturb customers, and the staff does not seem to take any responsibility to manage the situation. The worst part is the constant gutter smell, as the cafe is almost above a drain. Unfortunately, it feels like this issue will never be addressed due to negligence.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Hello Dipak Sapkale Koli, we sincerely apologize that your experience did not meet your expectations. The concerns you mentioned have been noted & we will surely look into this matter with our management team. Strict action will be taken regarding the issues you raised. Kindly share your contact details so that we can ensure improved service for you in the future.

featured_reviews.name: BEAST DESTROYER
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you enjoy your meals with a side of gutter aroma, Mani’s Cafe might just be your perfect spot. Food safety standards here feel more like a joke than a priority. While you’re trying to eat, don’t be surprised if beggars come over and disturb you—management clearly doesn’t see it as an issue.

Complaints? They’re heard, politely ignored, and taken completely for granted. Don’t expect any improvements either—nothing seems likely to change anytime soon.

Strongly recommend avoiding this place unless you’re in the mood for disappointment.

Only improvement that I feel is a place to sit while eating food. Generally people stand and eat but the food quality and the rates demand a suitable sitting place to enjoy the food better. featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jalaram's Tasty Ice Bhel in Mulund West and I must say, it exceeded my expectations. At Rs. 40, this street food snack is an absolute steal!

The ice bhel was a refreshing twist on the classic bhel puri, with a unique combination of sweet and savory flavors. The coolness of the cool icy chatni complemented the spicy and tangy flavors of the bhel perfectly, making for a delicious and satisfying snack.

The portion size was average, and the ingredients were fresh and flavorful. I especially loved the crunch of the sev and the juicy bursts of flavor from the pomegranate seeds.

The staff was friendly and attentive, and the stall was clean and well-maintained. Overall, Jai Jalaram's Tasty Ice Bhel is a must-try for anyone looking for a tasty and affordable street food snack in Mulund West. I highly recommend it!

The bhel was a perfect blend of moist and juicy ingredients, complemented by the rich flavors of date tamarind chutney and garlic chutney. The Pani Puri was a standout, offering a burst of flavors with amazing hot water, sprouts, and soaked boondi.

What truly impressed me was the affordability – at just 40 Rs. per plate, it's unquestionably a great value for money. The quality of ingredients and the attention to detail in preparation make Jai Jalaram Ice Bhel a go-to spot for those seeking a satisfying and budget-friendly street food experience. I highly recommend trying it for a delightful taste of authentic flavors without breaking the bank.

featured_reviews.name: Sayed Sana Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shameful & Disturbing Incident Outside Mani’s, Mulund (18th Oct 2025)
This review isn’t about food — it’s about basic humanity, which I saw completely missing outside Mani’s, Mulund West on the evening of 18th October 2025 (Saturday) during Diwali time.
While I was having dosa with my family, I witnessed something horrifying — a tall man in a kurta slapped and dragged a young beggar girl right outside the café. She must have been barely 10–12 years old. He hit her so hard, then grabbed her by her t-shirt and pulled her, while everyone just stood there and watched. It was one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen.
And what shocked me most — not one single person from Mani’s staff or management came forward. No one tried to stop that man or even check on that child. Everyone simply ignored it as if nothing happened. Even after assaulting her, that man came back to collect his parcel calmly while his wife sat in the car watching!
I want to ask Mani’s management — do your CCTV cameras not work? Did no staff member see this? Why didn’t anyone step up? It happened right at your doorstep. If you claim to be a family-friendly place, you also have a moral responsibility to protect people outside your premises, especially a child being assaulted in public view.
That moment made me lose all respect for this place. Good food means nothing when basic humanity and courage are missing. I truly hope Mani’s management takes this seriously, checks their CCTV footage from 18th October, identifies that man, and at least reports this inhuman act. Silence in such situations is shameful.

featured_reviews.name: MARATHWADA FOOD
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mukesh Pav Bhaji in Mulund West Khau Galli, which is a popular street food spot and seems quite well known among locals. The stall was busy when we visited, which usually indicates that people like the food here.
We ordered one pav bhaji priced around ₹100, and extra pav was ₹30. What I liked the most here was the pav. They serve a special masala pav, which is nicely toasted on the tawa with butter and masala. The pav was soft inside, slightly crispy outside, and had a good flavor. It was definitely the highlight of the dish.
The bhaji itself was decent but tasted a bit mild for my preference. It felt slightly on the bland side and not very spicy. It seemed like the gravy had a larger vegetable base and lighter masala. Some people may actually prefer this style because it feels less heavy and possibly uses fewer artificial flavor enhancers.
Overall, it is a good place to try once if you are exploring the street food in Mulund West Khau Galli. The masala pav is worth tasting.
Also, if you are already in the area, you can try pani puri at Gupta Panipuri Centre, which is located nearby in the pani puri galli. Their pani puri is quite popular among locals.

Street cafe , Located at Shree Nagar , Khau  galli .

Street cafe no doubt delivers some really yumm momos at very affordable rates. A good place to have some scrumptious momos without spending a lot!
Here we ordered :
Tandoori Gravy momos
For the new experience, we even try : Chicken Burger momos
Pizzza momos  [ Their speciality ]

Coming to taste here we can say momos were really mouthwatering .
Chicken Burger momos , Pizzza momos which we trying first time was amazing  in taste .
Size of the momos was also big , and filling was also in good quantity
Even we ordered pizza momos  for the 2nd time .
The staff was very friendly and the service was quick.
The place is awesome to give a shot for a new experience

Rating :
Food : 4.6 /5
Service : 4.9 / 5
Overall : 4.7 /5
